claim: Tongerlo Abbey houses a 34 m² Last Supper replica, painted under Da Vinci's supervision (likely by Andrea Solario, 1545); free admission; open Mon-Sat 08:00-11:00 and 13:00-17:00, Sundays 08:00-10:00 and 13:00-17:00.
quote: The painting can be viewed in the abbey church on weekdays (Monday - Saturday) from 8 to 11 am and from 1 to 5 pm and on Sundays from 8 to 10 am and from 1 to 5 pm. Admission is free.

claim: Tongerlo is a Norbertine (Premonstratensian) abbey founded c. 1130 and home to one of the most faithful surviving copies of Leonardo's Last Supper.
quote: Tongerlo Abbey (Dutch: Abdij van Tongerlo) is a Premonstratensian monastery in Tongerlo, in the municipality of Westerlo in the Belgian province of Antwerp.

claim: Kasteel de Merode in Westerlo is a private de Merode family residence; main rooms (knight's hall, drawing room, chapel) open to the public only during the annual Kasteelfeesten on the first weekend of July, otherwise by arranged guided tour.
quote: The most important rooms like the entrance hall, the 'ridderzaal' (knight's hall), the large drawing room, the dining room and the chapel can be visited during the 'Kasteelfeesten' in the first weekend of July.

claim: The Westerlo castle estate has a 12-ha English landscape park around the castle plus a 60-ha formal French-style park across the Grote Nete river.
quote: An English landscape park of 12 hectares surrounds the castle, and across the Nete river there is a larger formal park (60 hectares) in the French tradition with a rectangular pond forming a large perspective.

claim: Thirteen Flemish Béguinages — including Lier, Turnhout, Hoogstraten, Diest, Mechelen, Leuven and others — were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1998 as architectural ensembles of the Beguine movement.
quote: The Flemish Béguinages are architectural ensembles composed of houses, churches, ancillary buildings and green spaces, with a layout of either urban or rural origin and built in styles specific to the Flemish cultural region.

claim: The Diest beguinage, founded 1253, is a UNESCO-listed Flemish Béguinage with around 90 houses (mostly 17th-18th c.); the courtyard is freely accessible, with a bistro and shops inside; the Gothic Saint Catherine church anchors it.
quote: The Béguinage in Diest was founded in 1253, and most of the 90 houses were built during the 17th and 18th centuries. The Beguinage is freely accessible.

claim: Zimmertoren in Lier (with the famous Centenary Clock by Louis Zimmer) charges €8 adult / €3 youth (6-15) / free under 5; museum pass not accepted.
Zimmertoren is open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, closed Mondays and on 25 December and 1 January; visit takes 40-50 minutes with audio in NL/FR/DE/EN.
quote: The museum is open continuously from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 12:00 and from 13:00 to 17:00, and closed on Mondays.

claim: The Lier beguinage is a UNESCO-listed 13th-century street beguinage with 11 narrow streets and 95 houses; a new visitor centre in Begga's Court and Antonia's House opened October 2025.
quote: The beguinage in Lier has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998. It is a typical 13th century street beguinage with 11 narrow streets and 95 small houses.

claim: Turnhout's Kasteel van de Hertogen van Brabant (13th c., now a courthouse and classified monument since 1936) can only be visited with a guided tour booked at least three weeks in advance via Visit Turnhout, at €60 per guide plus a €5 admin fee; tour 1.5 h.
quote: Tours of the castle are only possible with a guide. You must reserve at least three weeks in advance via Visit Turnhout. The cost per guide is 60 euros, plus a one-time administrative fee of 5 euros.

claim: The Herentals Begijnhof (founded before 1266) is the oldest beguinage in the Kempen; courtyard always open; St Catherine's church (1614) and the small museum at no. 13 (former infirmary) only by guided tour.
quote: The begijnhof of Herentals was founded before 1266 and is the oldest begijnhof of the Kempen.

claim: Geel's Sint-Dimpnakerk (1349-1570, Demer-Gothic) is the pilgrimage church of St Dymphna, patron saint of mental illness, behind Geel's centuries-old tradition of community psychiatric care; contains a late-15th-c. carved-oak altarpiece and the de Merode mausoleum.
quote: The Church of St Dymphna, built in the period 1349-1570, is a beautiful example of the 'Demergothic' style.

claim: Aarschot's Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk is a Demer-Gothic ironstone church with a preserved late-Gothic Brabant choir screen and 'Mystical Wine Press' altarpiece; church and treasury open daily 09:00-12:00; tower climb (200 steps) reaches the Peace Carillon; admission free.
quote: The monumental Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk is built in Demer Gothic style. The church and treasury are open daily from 9 to 12 o'clock.

claim: Postel Abbey in Mol (north-east Kempen near the Dutch border) is a working Norbertine monastery occupied since 1140, with a Romanesque church, restored plague house, herb garden and famous library; grounds open most days outside services, guided tours via Mol tourist office.
quote: In the north-east corner of Mol, near the Dutch border, lies the Norbertine Postel Abbey. Norbertine monks have been living there since 1140.
